targets.label: STAGE 1 — THE DISCOUNT: eminence is already on from the command zone; a typed reducer stacks on top of it, and is NOT something this deck cannot function without
STAGE 2 — THE FLOOD: ramp that turns the discount into more than one Dragon a turn
STAGE 3 — THE BURN: a Dragon arriving or attacking becomes damage, or the damage it already deals is doubled
Protection held for the big turn
Dragon-restricted mana drawn (counts for nothing in mana_analysis, everything for casting a Dragon)
A Treasure source drawn — six in the 99, of which the model can SPEND only two
THE ENTRY KILL (UNVERIFIED — no passing stack): a per-dragon DAMAGE payoff AND a way to put several Dragons on the battlefield at once
THE COMBAT KILL (UNVERIFIED — no passing stack): a Dragon-damage MULTIPLIER AND a Dragon to attack with
The tempo layer: haste, an extra combat, or double strike on a Dragon that is already big
THE WHOLE MACHINE: discount AND flood AND burn AND a way to put several Dragons down at once

_note: Rewritten 2026-08-28 around the engine the pilot actually plays, in the three stages that make it: DISCOUNT (eminence from the command zone, permanent and unremovable, plus a typed reducer on top) -> FLOOD (ramp turning the discount into more than one Dragon a turn) -> BURN (a Dragon arriving or attacking becomes damage, and the doublers multiply it). The three are `required` because the deck is not doing its thing without all three; the previous declaration required ramp and a loosely-defined payoff, which nearly every game drew, so the engine lift compared two populations that were not different and spanned zero. Eminence itself is NOT a component: it needs no card, so no target can measure it.
_required_note: `required` marks the components this deck cannot function without; it is a JUDGEMENT, and the engine lift is what holds the judgement to account. MEASURED 2026-08-28 at 10,000 games, each stage split on its own, online by T5 against kill by T8: BURN +0.033 [+0.015, +0.051] REAL; FLOOD -0.006 [-0.027, +0.017]; DISCOUNT -0.028 [-0.044, -0.013] REAL. A second cost reducer drawn early correlates with a SLOWER kill, because eminence already pays the discount for free from the command zone and the reducer is a card and two-to-three mana that deals no damage. So STAGE 1 is declared and not required: it describes the deck honestly and does not get to define whether the engine is online. Requiring it made the whole engine figure anti-correlated with winning (-0.036 REAL), which is a finding about the DECLARATION, not about the deck. THE MODEL'S OWN LIMIT IS THE COUNTER-ARGUMENT AND IT IS REAL: card advantage is not modelled at all, so a reducer is charged its card and its mana and credited only with the discount, never with the extra spell a real turn casts. This split is correlational within one fixed list — it says games that drew a reducer early killed slower, NOT that cutting reducers makes the deck faster. `candidates` is what would say that.
